## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: for the anti-loop cap to work on the widened rule, the arming path must RECORD the red attempt (append the red-head marker line to the arm comment), so subsequent arms on the same head count toward the cap. The current arm_rework action doesn't record red-head markers (fail_validation does). So I need the arm_rework path used by this rule to:

For my widened rule, EVERY tick would re-match a red unchanged head after the label is consumed → the escalation would post EVERY TICK → comment spam. Need a once-per-head marker/anchor for the escalation.)

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: for the anti-loop cap to work on the widened rule, the arming path must RECORD the red attempt (append the red-head marker line to the arm comment), so subsequent arms on the same head count toward the cap. The current arm_rework action doesn't record red-head markers (fail_validation does). So I need the arm_rework path used by this rule to:
1. Read failMarkerState (redHeads[headSha]).

For my widened rule, EVERY tick would re-match a red unchanged head after the label is consumed → the escalation would post EVERY TICK → comment spam. /**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: for the anti-loop cap to work on the widened rule, the arming path must RECORD the red attempt (append the red-head marker line to the arm comment), so subsequent arms on the same head count toward the cap. The current arm_rework action doesn't record red-head markers (fail_validation does). So I need the arm_rework path used by this rule to:
1. Read failMarkerState (redHeads[headSha]).
2. If priorReds >= cap → withhold the arm + escalate to owner (once? — the fail path escalates every time at cap... let me check: reworkEmptyCapped posts the escalation comment EVERY time it fires. Hmm, but for the empty-lap cap the fail path only reaches the arm decision when fail-validation matches again, which happens per red verdict — each new red verdict is a new report. For my widened rule, EVERY tick would re-match a red unchanged head after the label is consumed → the escalation would post EVERY TICK → comment spam. Need a once-per-head marker/anchor for the escalation.)

Hmm wait, let me re-think. Actually, let me carefully trace the loop with my widened rule:

Tick 1: PR red, no labels → rule matches → arm_rework: latch consult (fresh) → gate → addLabel(PR, agent:rework) + comment + armReworkLatch. 
Tick 2: PR carries agent:rework → notLabels → rule quiet. rework-on-label (type pr, labels [agent:rework], consumeLabels [agent:rework]) → dispatch rework leg (PR-anchored), consume label.

Latch: terminated → clears (AC2). Red head unchanged → rule matches → arm again → dispatch again... 

INFINITE LOOP. Each cycle costs one AI leg. This is exactly "no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations".

And a head move (the leg pushed a fix — or any push) → new SHA → count resets by construction (markers keyed by SHA).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

Now I understand the marker machinery deeply. Let me now write the RCA and figure out the exact fix design.

## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: for the anti-loop cap to work on the widened rule, the arming path must RECORD the red attempt (append the red-head marker line to the arm comment), so subsequent arms on the same head count toward the cap. The current arm_rework action doesn't record red-head markers (fail_validation does). So I need the arm_rework path used by this rule to:
1. Read failMarkerState (redHeads[headSha]).
2. If priorReds >= cap → withhold the arm + escalate to owner (once? — the fail path escalates every time at cap... let me check: reworkEmptyCapped posts the escalation comment EVERY time it fires. Hmm, but for the empty-lap cap the fail path only reaches the arm decision when fail-validation matches again, which happens per red verdict — each new red verdict is a new report. For my widened rule, EVERY tick would re-match a red unchanged head after the label is consumed → the escalation would post EVERY TICK → comment spam. Need a once-per-head marker/anchor for the escalation.)

Hmm wait, let me re-think. Actually, let me carefully trace the loop with my widened rule:

Tick 1: PR red, no labels → rule matches → arm_rework: latch consult (fresh) → gate → addLabel(PR, agent:rework) + comment + armReworkLatch. 
Tick 2: PR carries agent:rework → notLabels → rule quiet. rework-on-label (type pr, labels [agent:rework], consumeLabels [agent:rework]) → dispatch rework leg (PR-anchored), consume label.
Tick 3: leg in flight (gh-715 cross-anchor guard / in-flight). Rule: notLabels agent:rework — label consumed → matches again! → arm_rework → consultReworkLatch → latched (leg in flight) → `continue` (quiet). Good — the latch suppresses.
Tick 4: leg concluded WITHOUT push (unfixable — e.g. method_size violations the agent can't fix without the full toolchain... hmm, actually the agent has the toolchain; the point is it closes without pushing). Latch: terminated → clears (AC2). Red head unchanged → rule matches → arm again → dispatch again... 

INFINITE LOOP. Each cycle costs one AI leg. This is exactly "no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations".

So the cap: on each arming decision for the SAME head, record a marker (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap); when prior count >= cap → withhold + escalate. With cap 3: arm→leg(∅)→arm→leg(∅)→arm→leg(∅)→then withhold+escalate. Hmm, actually: priorReds counts RECORDED reds. Tick1 arm records red 1/3. Tick4 arm records red 2/3. Tick7 arm records red 3/3. Tick10: priorReds=3 >= cap → withhold + escalate. So 3 legs then stop. That matches redHeadCap semantics (3 reds on the same head → validation waits for a NEW head).

And a head move (the leg pushed a fix — or any push) → new SHA → count resets by construction (markers keyed by SHA). 

Also the convergence-park analog: should the widened rule PARK validation_failed at the cap instead of just withholding? Hmm — the fail path's gh-832 park removes the PR from validate-armed's FIFO. For the dev-lane fresh PR (not approved), validate-armed doesn't apply anyway. The parked PR would match rework-on-validation-failed — wait, that rule matches validation_failed + red + machine → arm_rework! That would defeat the park for machine PRs... wait no — rework-on-validation-failed exists precisely to convert the machine parked latch into an arm ("the latched-park twin"). Hmm, so if my widened rule parked validation_failed at cap, the latched-park twin would immediately re-arm → loop. So NO park — the withhold+escalate (needs-human style) is the right terminal state for the machine lane... 

Hmm wait, hold on. Let me re-check rework-on-validation-failed's guards: labels [validation_failed], notLabels [agent:rework, ai_validating], checks [red], prMachineAuthor. Yes — a machine parked PR with red → arm_rework. It has NO cap of its own either! Could the unlatched rule + latched-park twin form a loop themselves for a machine PR?

Trace the EXISTING (pre-my-fix) machine-PR red-under-arm loop:
- validate-fresh arms ai_validating + dispatches quality (dispatch-only).
- Red. fail-validation (ai_validating+red): unarm, report (records 🔴 marker), machine: arm rework on linked issue (with gh-806 latch) — UNLESS reworkEmptyCapped (emptyLapMax empty laps → withhold + escalate).
- rework-on-red-ci (issue carrier agent:rework, notPrLabels agent:rework) → dispatch issue-anchored leg. The leg's post-action (pr_rework removeLabels) removes the label.
- Leg pushes fix → new head → validate-armed? No wait — the fresh dev PR is not approved. New head → checks none/pending → validate-fresh re-dispatches + arms. Etc.

The loop protection in the EXISTING flow: emptyLapMax + redHeadCap recorded in fail_validation. After redHeadCap reds recorded on the head, validate-armed skips re-arming (redHeadSkip) — but validate-fresh has NO redHeadSkip (query redHeadSkip — only validate-armed has `"redHeadSkip": true`)... and validate_pr's arm side "skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds" — the 🔴 red-head counter marker — "the validate_pr arm side skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds". Let me check validate_pr for the redHeadBlocked use.

OK regardless — the key point for MY fix: the widened arm path must (a) count arming attempts per head via the existing 🔴 marker convention, (b) withhold + escalate at redHeadCap. This gives "max attempts, no infinite retry".

Where to implement? Options:

Option 1: inside the arm_rework action in smAgent.js — but arm_rework is shared with rework-unresolved-threads (threads-driven). Adding a red-head-marker cap to the shared action would change that path too. For unresolved-threads, the "attempts" semantics differ (threads, not reds). Hmm. But recording 🔴 red-head markers from the threads path would be wrong (it's not a red verdict).

Option 2: a rule-scoped flag: `redHeadGated: true` on the widened rule — the action consults the cap only when the rule opts in. Clean, minimal, and the threads rule stays untouched.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the
 *   widened probe (legacy single-probe guard).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
 *   head_sha (any workflow/event/actor — the kicker's own push run included) that
 *   is active now or completed within this grace, and skips — its workflow_dispatch
 *   CI child may still be invisible to the event-filtered duplicate guard (Actions
 *   API registration lag; live fa ai/gh-1292: two CI runs 4s apart). 0 disables the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes (gh-917: PRs #413/#414 sat red 09:46Z/10:19Z → hand-fixed 11:19Z).

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 "a red pre-merge gate MUST arm a rework leg" rule) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` is stamped on the linked *issue* (dev leg), and `ai_validating` is only stamped by `validate-fresh` when it dispatches the validation CI — which never happens on an already-red head (`validate-fresh` matches checks `none`/`pending` only; `validate-fresh-masked-green` matches `green` only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label machine PR head matches nothing:

- `fail-validation` — no (needs `ai_validating`; the arm was never stamped),
- `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` — no (needs `ai_pr_reviewed`; never reviewed),
- `rework-on-validation-failed` — no (needs `validation_failed`; never parked),
- `validate-fresh` / `validate-fresh-masked-green` — no (need `none`/`pending`/`green`).

**Impact**: Any machine-authored PR whose first validation is red before its first review enters a permanent dead zone: no rework arm, no validation re-dispatch, SM ticks process nothing, the merge window stalls. Review-passed PRs (`ai_pr_reviewed`) are already covered by the 2026-10-15 rule (dart 408); only the pre-review first-validation wave is exposed.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to validation failures of ANY machine-authored PR (first validation included): drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement (a red wave with no arm must arm rework — latch or no latch, review or no review), keep the lane disjointness (`notLabels`: `ai_validating` → fail-validation owns the armed verdict; `validation_failed` → the latched-park twin owns it; `agent:rework` → already armed), and exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated, mirroring `validate-fresh`). Arm carrier = the PR label via the existing `arm_rework` action (`rework-on-label` dispatches the leg on the PR head; validation re-dispatch after the fix push is `validate-fresh`'s existing job). Anti-loop protections required by the ticket: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by `arm_rework`) plus a NEW `redHeadGated` max-attempts gate — the arm records the SAME 🔴 red-head marker history `fail_validation` writes (shared per-head budget) and at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the unchanged head the arm is WITHHELD and the owner is escalated once per head (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations; a head move resets the budget by construction).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

Now I understand the marker machinery deeply. Let me now write the RCA and figure out the exact fix design.

## RCA

**Bug**: A red FIRST validation (the quality wave) on a fresh machine-authored dev PR matches no SM rule — the SM tick concludes `processed: 0, skipped: 0` and the trunk stalls until a human intervenes.

**Root cause**: `sm_github.json` rule `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` (the OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-15 rule arming rework on red waves that reached the head OUTSIDE an armed validation) requires `labels: ["ai_pr_reviewed"]` — the post-review latch. A fresh dev PR (first validation, pre-review) carries NO PR labels: `ai_developed` goes on the linked issue, `ai_validating` is only stamped by validate-fresh when it dispatches the validation CI (which never happens on an already-red head — validate-fresh matches checks none/pending only, and validate-fresh-masked-green matches green only). So a red wave landing on a zero-label dev PR head matches:
- fail-validation: no (needs ai_validating),
- rework-on-red-gate-unlatched: no (needs ai_pr_reviewed),
- rework-on-validation-failed: no (needs validation_failed),
- validate-fresh / masked-green: no (need none/pending/green).

**Impact**: Machine-authored dev PRs whose first validation is red sit blocked forever; the merge window serializes behind nothing; the trunk stalls until a human fixes by hand.

**Fix approach**: Extend `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` to any machine-authored open PR (first validation included) — drop the `ai_pr_reviewed` requirement, keep the lane disjointness (notLabels ai_validating / validation_failed / agent:rework), exclude `chore:pin` (factory lockstep bumps stay factory-gated), and bound the arm with the same anti-loop protections: the gh-806 in-flight latch (already consulted by arm_rework) PLUS a max-attempt cap — the red-head marker history (🔴 red head <sha> — red N/cap) recorded on the PR: at `redHeadCap` (default 3) recorded reds on the same head, the arm is WITHHELD and the owner escalated (no infinite retry on unfixable-without-toolchain violations).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: for the anti-loop cap to work on the widened rule, the arming path must RECORD the red attempt (append the red-head marker line to the arm comment), so subsequent arms on the same head count toward the cap. The current arm_rework action doesn't record red-head markers (fail_validation does). So I need the arm_rework path used by this rule to:
1. Read failMarkerState (redHeads[headSha]).
2. If priorReds >= cap → withhold the arm + escalate to owner (once? — the fail path escalates every time at cap... let me check: reworkEmptyCapped posts the escalation comment EVERY time it fires. Hmm, but for the empty-lap cap the fail path only reaches the arm decision when fail-validation matches again, which happens per red verdict — each new red verdict is a new report. For my widened rule, EVERY tick would re-match a red unchanged head after the label is consumed → the escalation would post EVERY TICK → comment spam. Need a once-per-head marker/anchor for the escalation.)

Hmm wait, let me re-think. Actually, let me carefully trace the loop with my widened rule:

Tick 1: PR red, no labels → rule matches → arm_rework: latch consult (fresh) → gate → addLabel(PR, agent:rework) + comment + armReworkLatch. 
Tick 2: PR carries agent:rework → notLabels → rule quiet. rework-on-label (type pr, labels [agent:rework], consumeLabels [agent:rework]) → dispatch rework leg (PR-anchored), consume label.
Tick 3: leg in flight (gh-715 cross-anchor guard / in-flight). Rule: notLabels agent:rework — label consumed → matches again! → arm_rework → consultReworkLatch → latched (leg in flight) → `continue` (quiet). Good — the latch suppresses.
Tick 4: leg concluded WITHOUT push (unfixable — e.g. method_size violations the agent can't fix without the full toolchain... hmm, actually the agent has the toolchain; the point is it closes without pushing). Latch: terminated → clears (AC2). Red head unchanged → rule matches → arm again → dispatch again...

With cap 3: arm→leg(∅)→arm→leg(∅)→arm→leg(∅)→then withhold+escalate. Hmm, actually: priorReds counts RECORDED reds. Tick1 arm records red 1/3. Tick4 arm records red 2/3. Tick7 arm records red 3/3. Tick10: priorReds=3 >= cap → withhold + escalate. So 3 legs then stop. That matches redHeadCap semantics (3 reds on the same head → validation waits for a NEW head).

So NO park — the withhold+escalate (needs-human style) is the right terminal state for the machine lane...

The loop protection in the EXISTING flow: emptyLapMax + redHeadCap recorded in fail_validation. After redHeadCap reds recorded on the head, validate-armed skips re-arming (redHeadSkip) — but validate-fresh has NO redHeadSkip (query redHeadSkip — only validate-armed has `"redHeadSkip": true`)... and validate_pr's arm side "skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds" — the 🔴 red-head counter marker — "the validate_pr arm side skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds". But recording 🔴 red-head markers from the threads path would be wrong (it's not a red verdict).

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *   jobParams.cancelMaterializeTimeoutMs (default 45000, gh-848) — the
 *   twin-guard cancel polls a selected stale run until its jobs materialize
 *   (run.status != 'queued') up to this long before cancelling; still
 *   queued → the cancel is DEFERRED to the next tick. A queued cancel
 *   orphans the run's registered check-runs as `in_progress` ghosts that
 *   seize the merge gate forever (live fa #1457/#1520, ghosts #4-#6).
 *   0 restores the legacy cancel-immediately behavior. jobParams.
 *   cancelMaterializePollMs (default 3000, gh-848) — the poll interval.
 *   jobParams.dispatchRaceGraceMs (default 60000, gh-748) — how long a COMPLETED
 *   run on the head still counts as "may have just ordered CI" for the validate_pr
 *   dispatch-race guard: before dispatching, the arm also counts ANY run on the
